result.title: Reinforcing What the Student Has Learned: Teacher-Guided On-Policy Distillation
result.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) improves language-model reasoning through dense teacher feedback on student-generated responses.We first observe an amplitude disparity in this feedback: on math reasoning responses, style-related positions exhibit 3.5 times the mean absolute teacher--student log-probability difference of mathematical positions.Scaling OPD updates by these discrepancies thus directs much of the update strength toward matching the teacher's expression. We instead take the student's own pretrained base as a reference: the student--base difference records the token preferences acquired during post-training and provides supervision that does not depend on the student's distance from the teacher. Building on this reference, we propose Student-Delta On-Policy Distillation (SD-OPD), which uses centered student--base differences as update coefficients, keeps each coefficient only when its sign agrees with centered teacher--student feedback, and recomputes the student signal every training round. Across 5 teacher--student configurations with Qwen3 students of 1.7B to 8B parameters, SD-OPD improves six-task mathematics average pass@1 (avg@16) over OPD by 7.76 to 10.37 percentage points. Code is available at https://github.com/aim-uofa/sd-opd.

AI.brief_summary: 论文指出 on-policy distillation 的师生 log-prob 反馈存在幅度失衡，风格位置约为数学位置的 3.5 倍，并提出 SD-OPD：以中心化的「学生-预训练基座」差异作为更新系数，仅在符号与师生反馈一致时保留该系数，在 5 组 Qwen3 配置上提升数学平均 pass@1。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本方法，但其按 token 位置与符号一致性筛选监督信号、以基座差异刻画后训练所得偏好的做法，或可为 LVR 训练中的贡献分配、风格与任务必要内容区分提供可核查线索。
